messages:
customer-support: Heads-up: ACME private deployment seeing intermittent 403s + high tail latency when calling Redwood API through their VPC gateway. Started ~2026-03-16T03:05Z. App logs show KMS/HSM handshake failures and we have gaps in audit logs for the same window. Escalating for security/network review. @sanjay @maria

sanjay: thx. Any reproducible trace or short repro? Is this only for KMS-wrapped calls or all API traffic?

customer-support: Happens mostly on model inference calls (POST /v1/generate). Errors: `wrap key handshake failed` and client sees `403` from our edge. They also reported retries spiking which increased latency and costs. Attached minimal logs: `2026-03-16T03:06:12Z ERROR: kms: handshake failed err=TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate`

maria: do we have audit log ids for the missing entries? Need to know if logs were dropped at collector or never emitted by control plane.

customer-support: sample request id: `req_45a7f`. We see no audit entry for that id in the retention store between 03:05-03:10.

iris: can you paste a small tcpdump from the customer's NAT/gateway for the failing window? look for TLS SNI and dest IPs.

customer-support: forwarded pcap excerpt from customer. tcpdump shows TLS ClientHello SNI: `redwood-internal.kms-prod` for some flows, but a subset of flows have SNI `null` (no SNI) and are being reset by their firewall. snippet: ```
14:23:12.345678 IP 10.0.5.21.34567 > 54.239.10.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
14:23:12.346999 TLS ClientHello, SNI: redwood-internal.kms-prod
14:23:12.347222 TLS ClientHello, no SNI
```

kevin: that looks like their TLS proxy is doing SNI stripping for some client flows. Most HSM/KMS provisioning requires SNI intact for routing to HSM clusters. If SNI is removed the upstream may reject with handshake error -> client gets 403. Also retries can trigger rate-limiting which produces missing audit entries.

devops-bot: deploy:control-plane v2.14 rolled at 2026-03-16T02:50Z to hosted API nodes. No related incidents flagged.

security-oncall: assigning to network/security triage. @maria can you confirm required egress rules for Private deployments and HSM/KMS endpoints (ports, SNI exceptions, IP ranges)?

maria: yes. Required: outbound HTTPS (443) to KMS endpoints and HSM clusters, preserve SNI, allow ephemeral client ports (32768-61000) return traffic, and ensure NAT conntrack sizing: on heavy retry bursts conntrack exhaustion drops flows causing missing audit writes. Also keep audit collector endpoints reachable on 443.

sanjay: ask customer to temporarily bypass TLS proxy (if possible) or enable SNI passthrough for Redwood endpoints and retest. Also request `netstat -an | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l` and `conntrack -S` output if available.

customer-support: customer ran quick tests. After enabling SNI passthrough for `*.redwood-internal.kms-prod` the failures dropped to 0 for 15m. They also sent `conntrack -S` showing dentry count at 250k (their conntrack table max 262k).

kevin: that explains intermittent resets. When conntrack is near limit the kernel starts dropping new flows. Retries cause burst of new connections to KMS which either never make it to our control plane (missing audit entries) or hit rate limits producing 403s.

iris: we should provide a short runbook patch for customers: 1) ensure SNI passthrough for Redwood endpoints 2) open ephemeral port range for return traffic 3) increase conntrack to recommended minimum (512k) or use connection reuse/pinning. Include the quick tcpdump/curl checks.

maria: also flag that some corporate firewalls rewrite TLS and may strip SNI for TLS 1.2 flows. Recommend customers move to TLS 1.3 or ensure proxy preserves SNI header.

customer-support: shared a reproducible curl showing failure when SNI stripped: ```
# failing (no sni)
curl -v --resolve "redwood-internal.kms-prod:443:54.239.10.12" https://redwood-internal.kms-prod/v1/wrap -H 'Host: redwood-internal.kms-prod' --tlsv1.2
# success (sni preserved)
curl -v --tlsv1.3 https://redwood-internal.kms-prod/v1/wrap
```

maria: regarding audit logs — once flows reach control plane they get queued for audit. If the connection never succeeds we won't receive the event. We should document that missing audit entries in a time window correlate with network-level resets. Recommend customer retain full packet capture for the window and share pcap if they want deeper forensics.

security-oncall: any KMS key policy concerns? Could the handshake fail be a key policy reject?

sanjay: unlikely given repro with SNI passthrough. But still ask customer to validate KMS key ARN and key policy and share a sanitized `aws kms` request flow if they changed key rotation recently.

kevin: I'll draft the firewall config snippet for them to paste into their gateway appliance (example shown for Palo Alto / Cisco ASA): ```
# Example: allow outbound SNI-pass-through for Redwood endpoints
policy id 210 allow from inside to INTERNET service https 
  match host *.redwood-internal.kms-prod
  preserve-tls-sni yes
# increase conntrack on linux
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
```

customer-support: customer applied `preserve-sni` change and bumped conntrack to 524288. They reported immediate improvement, no 403s after 20m and audit entries for previously missing req ids appeared.

maria: action items: 1) update private deployment docs troubleshooting section with SNI/pass-through note, conntrack guidance, and minimal curl/tcpdump checks. 2) send runbook snippet to support templates. 3) follow up with customer to confirm long-term config.

sanjay: also add a note in the on-call playbook about checking conntrack saturation when seeing missing audit logs.

security-oncall: thanks team. Closing initial triage. If customer requests deeper forensics we'll reopen and request full pcap + key policy extract. :white_check_mark:

customer-support: customer very happy. Marking as resolved on our side and sharing docs link once updated.
